title: Access Loom: policy runtime, decision cache and proxy adapter for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Current RBAC behaviour is fragmented across API gateway, runtime serving, and console. We need a single policy evaluation runtime and lightweight proxy adapter that provides consistent allow/deny semantics, explainability for deny reasons, and an auditable decision stream for compliance.

Goal: Ship a production-ready policy runtime ("Access Loom") + a proxy adapter for the API/runtime/console that: 1) evaluates RBAC v2 policies with low p99 latency (target <= 2ms local eval, <=7ms distributed), 2) supports a decision cache for hot tokens and prefix-KV reuse, 3) emits an immutable, structured audit decision record to the Audit Sink, and 4) integrates SSO/SAML admin metadata for role bindings and session context.

Scope: Core policy evaluator, decision cache layer, authorization proxy adapter (sidecar and sidecarless modes), audit record schema and sink integration, SSO attribute enrichment path, migration shim for existing check hooks. Does NOT include full UI for role editing (console team will own that in a follow-up), but includes API hooks for the console to consume decisions and explanations.
acceptance_criteria: New policy runtime serves evaluation API with TLS and mTLS support and passes interop tests with existing policy repo
P99 decision latency: <=7ms for remote eval; <=2ms for cached/local eval under 95th percentile load profile
Audit records emitted for every decision with unique decision_id, policy_version, principal_context, request_context and signed integrity hash
Explainable deny field present in response (reason_code + human_message + policy_path) and surfaced to Console via API
Migration shim toggled via feature-flag; can run in parallel to legacy gating with shadow mode capturing telemetry
SSO session attributes (groups, org_id, admin_claims) are available to policy evaluator and stored in audit stream
design_notes:
Design uses a deterministic evaluator core (policy-loom) compiled from declarative RBAC v2 JSON into an optimized evaluation DAG. Evaluation DAG nodes are AOT-compiled to avoid allocations on the hot path. Decision cache is a two-layer cache: local LRU per-proxy for microsecond hits and a distributed compact indexed cache (delta-updates via policy-change stream) for warm hits. Policies are versioned and pinned in the runtime; policy deltas are streamed via admin-led policy broadcaster.

Authorization proxy adapter runs in two modes: sidecar (per-service) and sidecarless (gateway-level). The adapter emits a blocking decision to callers when required, and can attach an X-Decision header for downstream debugging. All adapters sign decisions with key material sourced from KMS. Audit records are batched and written to the audit sink with at-least-once semantics and idempotency via decision_id de-duplication.

Explainability leverages a policy_path breadcrumb that references rule IDs and human-friendly messages stored in policy metadata. For privacy, sensitive fields are redacted before emitting audit records when policy indicates PII presence.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): evaluator core (in Go), local LRU cache, policy delta consumer, simple HTTP/gRPC proto, tests. Phase 2 (3 sprints): adapter sidecar, audit sink wiring (Kafka->audit-processor), decision signing, SSO attribute enrichment via session introspector. Phase 3 (2 sprints): sidecarless gateway adapter, rollout canary, feature flag, performance tuning and kernel-level CPU affinity experiments.

Key milestones: unit/integration tests by sprint end, load test run on staging with 10k RPS workload, security review completed before canary rollout, compliance sign-off for immutable audit retention config.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flagged shadow mode: route 100% traffic to legacy gate, run Access Loom in shadow and capture diffs for 3 days. 2) Canary: 1% of production calls with full blocking enabled in a low-impact customer subset, collect analytics for 7 days. 3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on policy-mismatch or p95 latency regression. 4) Post-cutover: deprecate legacy hooks and flip migration flag during off-peak window.

Admin controls: only tenants with 'policy_migration' permission in admin console can opt-in to canary. Rollback path includes kill-switch at control-plane route and cached-policy expunge endpoint.
telemetry_and_metrics: Decision latency (p50/p95/p99), cache hit ratio (local/distributed), policy-version skew, shadow-diff rate, explainability coverage (percent of denies with explanation), audit throughput and backpressure metrics, decision-signing error rate. Emit traces for decision evaluation and adapter proxy path. Add cost metric: compute tokens-per-decision to correlate cost with batching settings.
